items.title: Jim H. Dunbar Jr. Interview, 1959-11-28
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Alden Ashworth; the name is only introduced by the interviewer as someone who spent time with Bill Russell.

ctx.x: People, I think, talk about what is Bill Russell, trying to figure out why he likes it, why he likes this mystery. Because you tend to think, well, there's got to be, Bill has to have some, Bill has a story, there must have been some tragedy or unrequited love or some great plan that ran awry and caused Bill to kind of ignore the rest of humanity. Because it's not fair of me to say this because my, you know, relationship with Bill has been almost non-existent. I don't see Bill that often, but what I, what you…

Well, I think Bill was married once, but I've never been able to get the story on that straight. But Alden and David, Alden Ashworth and David Wyckoff, two guys I knew, were down here. And spent a lot of time with Bill. Say that, that he was married, but they don't know any of the details. But I'm sure if he was married, it was to some classical musician, some woman, probably some violin player like him. Was interested in composing a couple of things, probably had a lot in common. Still, it didn't work out on an…
I wonder about Bill's violin playing. Because Bill is, if there's anything Bill is, about music, he's serious about it.
